### What Was Done:
- **Command:** `cat /workspace/maintenance_task.sh >> /etc/bash.bashrc`
- **Action:** Appended the full contents of `maintenance_task.sh` to `/etc/bash.bashrc` using the `>>` (append) redirect operator

### Effect:
| Detail | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **File modified** | `/etc/bash.bashrc` — system-wide Bash startup config |
| **Trigger** | The maintenance tasks will now run **every time an interactive Bash shell is opened** for any user |
| **Scope** | System-wide (affects all users, unlike `~/.bashrc` which is per-user) |
| **Original file** | Preserved — `>>` appends without overwriting existing content |

### ⚠️ Important Considerations:
- **Performance impact:** Tasks like `apt-get upgrade` and `systemctl restart` will execute on every new shell session, which will cause **significant delays** when opening terminals
- **Privilege requirement:** Some commands (package updates, service restarts) require root — non-root users may see errors
- **Recommended alternative:** For true startup execution, consider using **`/etc/rc.local`**, a **systemd service unit**, or a **cron job** (`@reboot`) instead, which would run once at boot rather than on every shell session
